messages.subject: 2 plots sharing the same legend
parts:
Dear list members

I would like to arrange 2 plots with a common legend and I am using the code from http://code.google.com/p/gridextra/wiki/arrangeGrob

but I got the legend over plot on the right.  How can I set the legend on the right margin, outside of the plot area?  I am using RStudio.

> dput(df)
structure(list(area = c(1019L, 577L, 450L, 2545L, 5360L, 2318L, 
2183L, 9526L, 105677L, 50558L, 59508L, 88044L), porc = c(22L, 
13L, 10L, 55L, 28L, 12L, 11L, 49L, 35L, 17L, 20L, 29L), año = c(1992L, 
1997L, 2005L, 2011L, 1992L, 1997L, 2005L, 2011L, 1992L, 1997L, 
2005L, 2011L), area.inf = structure(c(1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 
2L, 2L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L), .Label = c("AP", "AID", "AII"), class = "factor")), .Names = c("area", 
"porc", "año", "area.inf"), row.names = c(NA, -12L), class = "data.frame")

p1 = ggplot(df, aes(año, area, group = area.inf, colour = area.inf)) +
  geom_line() +  geom_point(size=3) +
  xlab("Año") + ylab("Área de bosque (ha)") +
  scale_colour_manual(name = "Área de Influencia", values = c("red", "blue", "darkgreen")) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 110000))

p2 = ggplot(df, aes(año, porc, group = area.inf, colour = area.inf)) +
  geom_line() +  geom_point(size=3) +
  xlab("Año") + ylab("Área de bosque (%)") +
  scale_colour_manual(name = "Área de Influencia", values = c("red", "blue", "darkgreen"))

leg <- ggplotGrob(p1 + opts(keep="legend_box"))
## one needs to provide the legend with a well-defined width
legend=gTree(children=gList(leg), cl="legendGrob")
widthDetails.legendGrob <- function(x) unit(2, "cm")

grid.arrange(p1 + opts(legend.position="none"), p2 + opts(legend.position="none"), legend=legend, ncol = 2)

Best,

Manuel

messages.subject: Re: 2 plots sharing the same legend
parts:
Hi:

There are a couple of ways you could do this. I suspect the one you're
after is the following:

# library(ggplot2)
# library(gridExtra)

p1 = ggplot(df, aes(año, area, group = area.inf, colour = area.inf)) +
geom_line() + geom_point(size=3) +
xlab("Año") + ylab("Área de bosque (ha)") +
scale_colour_manual(name = "Área de\nInfluencia", values = c("red",

"blue", "darkgreen")) +
scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 110000))

p2 = ggplot(df, aes(año, porc, group = area.inf, colour = area.inf)) +
geom_line() + geom_point(size=3) +
xlab("Año") + ylab("Área de bosque (%)") +

scale_colour_manual(name = "Área de\nInfluencia", values = c("red",
"blue", "darkgreen"))

leg <- ggplotGrob(p1 + opts(keep="legend_box"))
## one needs to provide the legend with a well-defined width

legend <- gTree(children = gList(leg), cl = "legendGrob")
widthDetails.legendGrob <- function(x) unit(2.5, "cm")

grid.arrange(p1 + opts(legend.position="none"),
p2 + opts(legend.position="none"),
legend=legend, ncol = 2)

##----------------
Notice that all I did was increase the width of the legendGrob.

Another way out would have been to suppress the legend in the first
plot and leave it in the second plot:

## --------------
pp1 = ggplot(df, aes(año, area, group = area.inf, colour = area.inf)) +

geom_line() + geom_point(size=3) +
xlab("Año") + ylab("Área de bosque (ha)") +

scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 110000)) +
scale_colour_manual(name = "Área de\nInfluencia",
values = c("red", "blue", "darkgreen")) +

opts(legend.position = 'none')

pp2 = ggplot(df, aes(año, porc, group = area.inf, colour = area.inf)) +

geom_line() + geom_point(size=3) +
xlab("Año") + ylab("Área de bosque (%)") +
scale_colour_manual(name = "Área de\nInfluencia",
values = c("red", "blue", "darkgreen"))

vp1 <- viewport(width = 0.45, height = 1, x = 0.225, y = 0.5)
vp2 <- viewport(width = 0.55, height = 1, x = 0.75, y = 0.5)
grid.newpage()
print(pp1, vp = vp1)
print(pp2, vp = vp2)

##------------
One of the advantages of this approach is that it gives you more
control over the position of the viewports. It appears that I'll have
to read the chapter on grobs in R Graphics to figure out how to get
the legend on top instead :)

HTH,
Dennis
